title: The Nightly Cinema
narration: [whisper] Every night, you direct a film you’ll never remember. Your brain burns as much energy as when awake. So why this private screening?
visual_goal: A person asleep, but brain glowing with cinematic film reel overlays; energy waves pulsating.

title: Discovery in a Basement
narration: In 1953, in a basement lab at Chicago, Aserinsky and Kleitman spotted darting eyes behind closed lids. They’d discovered REM sleep — the dream stage.
visual_goal: Vintage 1950s lab, scientist observing a sleeping volunteer, close-up of eyes moving rapidly, old EEG machine with squiggles.

title: Freud’s Wish Fulfillment
narration: Decades earlier, in 1899, Freud declared dreams were wish fulfillment — forbidden desires smuggled onto the night’s screen. A theory that held for years. [sigh]
visual_goal: Old book of Freud, smoke and mirrors, a theater curtain opening to reveal a hidden desire symbol.

title: The REM Rollercoaster
narration: Tonight, you’ll voyage into REM four to five times. Each phase grows longer, the final one stretching up to forty-five minutes — your brain’s longest feature.
visual_goal: Animated cycle of REM stages, clock ticking, a graph showing increasing REM duration, a person in deep sleep with lengthening REM bar.

title: The Great Erasure
narration: [gasp] But here’s the twist: ninety-five percent of your dreams vanish within minutes of waking. They dissolve like vapor — why would your brain erase its own masterpiece?
visual_goal: Alarm clock ringing, dream imagery shattering into pixels, a person looking confused, morning light streaming, evaporating dreams.

title: The Dimmer Dreams
narration: Dreams also flicker during non-REM sleep, but they’re dimmer — fragments, not feature films. The full reel only spins in REM. Less story, more mood.
visual_goal: Split screen: REM side vivid colors, NREM side muted, shadowy figures, a projector dimming, fragments of scenes.

title: The Random Static Theory
narration: In 1977, Hobson and McCarley dropped a bombshell: dreams are just random static from your brainstem, stitched into a story by your frontal lobes. No hidden meaning. [chuckle]
visual_goal: Brainstem highlighted, static TV noise, frontal lobe stitching images together like film editing.

title: Sleep Makes You Smarter
narration: Yet sleeping after learning a task doubles your chance of finding hidden rules. The dreaming brain connects dots the waking mind ignores — a silent problem-solver.
visual_goal: Person learning, then sleeping, then waking with a lightbulb moment, solving a puzzle.

title: Overnight Therapy
narration: [sigh] REM sleep also strips the sharp edges off emotional memories, a kind of overnight therapy. By dawn, yesterday’s sting feels softer.
visual_goal: Emotional memory: a cry, then a soft sunrise, a calmed person waking up, heart rate calming.

title: The Director’s Chair & The Real Show
narration: And about half of us have hijacked the director’s chair at least once [chuckle] — lucid dreaming, fully aware inside the show. So why the nightly cinema? To rehearse threats, untangle emotions, and solve problems silently. Your brain runs the projector so when you wake, you’re ready for the real show.
visual_goal: Lucid dreamer controlling dream, flying; then brain rehearsal of scenarios, then waking up refreshed ready for the day, last shot: person opening eyes with a smile, cinematic fade out.
